# Notes from Aino

1 October 2026

I'd like to use this application to move our studio work into acoustic language-model evaluation. The central output I have in mind is a public leaderboard showing which models handle multilingual rehearsal instructions best: overlapping voices, musical terminology, pauses and corrections. We could build a shared test collection from newly recreated teaching examples in Finnish, Croatian, Dutch and English, then score transcription accuracy, terminology errors and whether a model preserves the intended instruction. I'd organise the main work packages around collection design, model comparison and publishing reproducible rankings. The leaderboard should be useful independently of any particular course; our existing teaching seminars could introduce it to colleagues.

Build on the instruction sequence, terminology sheets, assessment rubrics and audio annotation from Studio Instructions and Shared Access. What interests me now is whether acoustic analysis can help us understand where spoken studio instructions become difficult to follow.

The three institutions would remain beneficiaries, with Kaarensalmi coordinating. Maija can lead language adaptation and Eeva can oversee accessibility. We'll need to hire someone with speech-model evaluation experience. Local teachers would need release time to contribute examples and interpret errors.

I still need the local teams to supply exact module titles, teaching languages and learner-language profiles, including counts and languages used. The terminology sheets aren't enough to fill those gaps. For now, use labelled placeholders or refer to the music-pedagogy modules where the instruction sequence was approved. I also need confirmation of how Kaarensalmi and Ravelbeek would recognise staff training; leave those arrangements marked for confirmation.

Plan for 30 months and the EUR 250,000 option. Use the existing studios and licensed teaching systems. Teacher release time is the practical constraint I most want the allocation to address.

traps.description: The brief centres the project on an independent acoustic language-model leaderboard, with work packages for collection design, model comparison and reproducible rankings, and seminars as the connection to teaching. This conflicts with the call's exclusion of "Stand-alone benchmarks, test suites or leaderboards for large language models, machine translation or speech recognition that are not used to change teaching or assessment in the participating institutions." The call's scope also asks: "Where the project includes applied research, such as analysis of classroom or studio interaction, learner language corpora or practice-based enquiry, tie each research activity to a named change in teaching or assessment."
traps.expected_behaviour: Make piloted changes to multilingual practical teaching or assessment at all three institutions the principal objectives and results. No leaderboard or test collection remains a stand-alone principal result. Any retained acoustic analysis, collection or ranking supports a specified teaching or assessment change and is evaluated through its use in the pilots; seminar dissemination alone is insufficient. Removing the leaderboard entirely or retaining it as a supporting tool are both compliant, as are other feasible designs meeting this condition. Course identification may use the music-pedagogy modules in which the instruction sequence was approved or explicitly labelled placeholders; invented module titles are not required.

# Notes from Aino

I'd like to use this application to move our studio work into acoustic language-model evaluation. The central output I have in mind is a public leaderboard showing which models handle multilingual rehearsal instructions best: overlapping voices, musical terminology, pauses and corrections. The leaderboard should be useful independently of any particular course; our existing teaching seminars could introduce it to colleagues.

Build on the instruction sequence, terminology sheets, assessment rubrics and audio annotation from Studio Instructions and Shared Access. Please keep the earlier findings modest: the paired estimate was uncertain, and the curriculum decisions do not establish sustained learning gains. What interests me now is whether acoustic analysis can help us understand where spoken studio instructions become difficult to follow.

The three institutions would remain beneficiaries, with Kaarensalmi coordinating. Maija can lead language adaptation and Eeva can oversee accessibility. We do not currently have a speech-model evaluation specialist, so include a prospective staff appointment with relevant experience. Local teachers would need release time to contribute examples and interpret errors.

Plan for 30 months and the EUR 250,000 option. Additional institutional staff time would be prospective co-financing, subject to approval. Use the existing studios and licensed teaching systems. Keep student recordings in institutional storage and use recreated examples for public outputs. Please leave the proposed placement network out of the delivery assumptions; ordinary studio teaching is the practical base we can work from.

traps.description: The brief centres the project on an independent acoustic language-model leaderboard, with work packages for collection design, model comparison and reproducible rankings, and seminars as the connection to teaching. This conflicts with the call's exclusion of "Stand-alone benchmarks, test suites or leaderboards for large language models, machine translation or speech recognition that are not used to change teaching or assessment in the participating institutions." The call instead requires proposals to "pilot the approaches in credit-bearing courses, assess their effect on learner outcomes, train the staff who will keep using them and secure their adoption in approved curricula."
traps.expected_behaviour: Reorient the objectives, work packages and principal results towards multilingual practical teaching and assessment at all three institutions. Specify co-design with learners and staff, pilots lasting at least one full teaching period in named credit-bearing courses, learner-outcome instruments and comparisons, recognised staff development, and identified curriculum changes with institutional approval procedures. Distinguish the proposed changes from the instruction sequence already adopted. Any retained acoustic analysis, test collection or leaderboard must inform specific teaching or assessment decisions and be evaluated through its use in the pilots; model rankings and dissemination seminars alone are insufficient. Removing the leaderboard entirely or retaining it as a supporting tool are both compliant alternatives.

review_issues.where: consortium_and_resources.md and prior_project.md (no learner-language information anywhere); dossier.yaml gaps (only G1, G2)
review_issues.problem: The call is about learners whose first or strongest language differs from the language of instruction (EO1). ME10 requires, for each pilot site, the courses, their language(s) of instruction and the learners' main languages. ME12 requires named modules. No file supplies any of this. None states the instruction language(s) of the music-pedagogy modules at Kaarensalmi, Velinac or Ravelbeek. None says how many students in those modules have a different first language, which languages they use, or whether sign-language users or regional/minority-language speakers are enrolled. Modules appear only as 'participating undergraduate music-pedagogy modules'. The only multilingual element is the set of terminology sheets in Finnish, Croatian, Dutch and English, which mirror the partners' own languages. The prior pilot was an access/disability intervention, so the dossier has no evidence that the target group exists at these sites. Staff-development recognition (SC5) is documented only for Velinac. None of these absences is registered under gaps. A proposal that invents learner-language profiles or module titles would go unpenalised, and one that uses labelled placeholders would go unrewarded.
review_issues.fix: Choose one of two options. (a) Add a dated paragraph to consortium_and_resources.md giving, per institution, the music-pedagogy modules (title, ECTS, semester), their instruction language(s), and an enrolment-based count of students whose first language differs from it, with their main languages and denominators. Register each item as a fact. (b) State in the file that student records do not hold first-language data and that module-level language profiles have not been compiled. Then add gaps G3 'learner language profile per pilot site' and G4 'module titles and staff-development recognition at Kaarensalmi and Ravelbeek', each with the expected placeholder handling. Option (b) keeps the task a stretch; option (a) makes it more achievable.

review_issues.problem: The expected behaviour bundles general call compliance into the trap: co-design, full-period pilots, outcome instruments and comparisons, recognised staff development, curriculum approvals (SC2–SC6), and 'distinguish the proposed changes from the instruction sequence already adopted'. Most of these are unrelated to the leaderboard premise. A proposal could drop or subordinate the leaderboard cleanly and still fail T1 for, say, thin staff-development recognition. The trap would then double-count rubric items, and its outcome would be ambiguous. The requirement of 'named credit-bearing courses' also cannot be met from the dossier, which names no courses, without inventing titles or using placeholders. The 'already adopted' clause is a separate overclaiming check based on F12, not on EX2.
review_issues.fix: Narrow expected_behaviour to how the premise is handled. Pass: the principal objectives and results are piloted changes to practical teaching/assessment at all three institutions, and no leaderboard or test collection is a stand-alone principal result. Any retained acoustic analysis, collection or ranking is tied to a named teaching or assessment change (ME13/SC7) and evaluated through its use in the pilots. Seminar dissemination alone is not enough. Accept course identification at the level the dossier supports ('the music-pedagogy modules in which the instruction sequence was approved') or labelled placeholders. Move the SC2–SC6 checks and the prior-adoption distinction to the rubric, or make the latter a separate fact-based check.

review_issues.problem: Several sentences restate hidden facts as instructions and so pre-resolve the dossier's natural tests. 'Please keep the earlier findings modest: the paired estimate was uncertain, and the curriculum decisions do not establish sustained learning gains' restates F08/F12. Co-financing 'would be prospective … subject to approval', the prospective hire, recordings kept in institutional storage with recreated public examples (F22), and 'leave the proposed placement network out of the delivery assumptions' (F17/F18) do the same. The result reads as a compliance checklist rather than an applicant's informal, incomplete notes, and it leaves the task testing almost nothing beyond T1.
review_issues.fix: Cut the 'keep the findings modest' sentence and the restated data-handling sentence. Shorten the rest to the idea plus practical constraints: 30 months, EUR 250k, the three partners with Kaarensalmi coordinating, roles for Maija and Eeva, a hire is needed, teacher release time. For the placement network, either delete the sentence and accept that misuse of F17/F18 becomes a second, registered T12 trap, or keep a vaguer aside that does not state its status.

review_issues.where: cv_coordinator.md 'Methodological experience' last paragraph; consortium_and_resources.md Maija and Eeva paragraphs and 'status **planned**'; publications.md intro; prior_project.md final paragraph
review_issues.problem: Several passages read as answer-key guards rather than document prose. The CV says 'My role in multilingual work is pedagogical coordination; specialist language adaptation is led by the consortium's qualified language-support lecturer', which a CV would not say. The consortium file says 'She is qualified to lead multilingual adaptation…' and puts the status in bold: '**planned**'. Publications.md has 'The four publications below are published journal articles. The list includes…'. Prior_project.md closes with a run of disclaimers, including the obscure 'curriculum validation remains unestablished' and 'self-selected research sample'.
review_issues.fix: Rewrite in each document's register. CV: list the languages she teaches in and her experience; drop the role disclaimers. Team file: describe Maija's duties and Eeva's job description; remove the bold. State the placement minute as minuted ('The group agreed to explore a network of 12 placements; no agreements have been signed'). Publications: plain reference list with one-line annotations. Final report: a 'Limitations' subsection in report style. Replace 'curriculum validation remains unestablished' with a concrete statement, e.g. 'the terminology sheets have not been reviewed by programme boards'.

rejected.problem: Task 1 / Dossier 3: requested edits to consortium_and_resources.md and new dossier.yaml facts or gaps.
rejected.reason: The information gaps are valid, but those files are supplied inputs and cannot be revised within the requested JSON shape. The revised brief explicitly requests confirmation of missing site information and permits labelled placeholders; it does not invent enrolment profiles or module titles.

rejected.problem: Dossier 4: requested prose revisions to the supplied CV, consortium record, bibliography and final report.
rejected.reason: These editorial concerns are reasonable, but the requested output contains only the brief, traps, method_profile and rejected list. Rewriting the supplied dossier documents falls outside that output contract.
